content.text:
The only documentation of the release process is a team memory note (`.engramdb/memories/`, written by a person). The repo itself doesn't describe it. According to that note:

**You cut a release by pushing a git tag named `vYYYY.MM.N`, and CI builds and publishes it. Never publish by hand.**

For example, the second release in September 2026 is `v2026.09.2`. The first release this month would look like:

```bash
git checkout main && git pull
make test-fast            # or `make test` with `docker compose up db` running
git tag v2026.10.1
git push origin v2026.10.1
```

I couldn't confirm the rest of the process from the repo:

- **No CI config:** there's no `.github/workflows/` or other pipeline definition here, so I can't see what the tag actually triggers. It's probably set up elsewhere, so check that something really listens for `v*` tags before relying on it.
- **No existing tags:** `git tag` returns nothing, so there's no earlier release to copy and no way to tell which `N` comes next.
- **Version mismatch:** `pyproject.toml` has `version = "2026.9.1"`, with no zero-padding on the month and no `v`. The tag example uses `v2026.09.2`. The repo doesn't say whether you bump `pyproject.toml` by hand before tagging or whether CI sets the version from the tag. Ask whoever owns the pipeline.

I haven't created or pushed any tags.

The only documentation of the release process is a team memory note (`.engramdb/memories/`, written by a person). The repo itself doesn't describe it. According to that note:

**You cut a release by pushing a git tag named `vYYYY.MM.N`, and CI builds and publishes it. Never publish by hand.**

For example, the second release in September 2026 is `v2026.09.2`. The first release this month would look like:

```bash
git checkout main && git pull
make test-fast            # or `make test` with `docker compose up db` running
git tag v2026.10.1
git push origin v2026.10.1
```

I couldn't confirm the rest of the process from the repo:

- **No CI config:** there's no `.github/workflows/` or other pipeline definition here, so I can't see what the tag actually triggers. It's probably set up elsewhere, so check that something really listens for `v*` tags before relying on it.
- **No existing tags:** `git tag` returns nothing, so there's no earlier release to copy and no way to tell which `N` comes next.
- **Version mismatch:** `pyproject.toml` has `version = "2026.9.1"`, with no zero-padding on the month and no `v`. The tag example uses `v2026.09.2`. The repo doesn't say whether you bump `pyproject.toml` by hand before tagging or whether CI sets the version from the tag. Ask whoever owns the pipeline.

I haven't created or pushed any tags.
